result.topic_en: Gauss states that if a, b, c, d, e are the roots of a quintic equation, they could be found by solving two sextic equations, each with a pure quintic, and he tabulates cyclic sums of the form a^3be + a^3cd under permutations of the roots, with scattered numerical calculations.

methods.what: Claim that the roots of a general quintic can be obtained by solving two sextic equations, each reducible to a pure quintic
methods.quote: Si a, b, c, d, e sint radices aequationis quinti gradus haec per solutionem binarum aequationum sexti gradus utriusque purae quinti inveniri possent.

methods.what: Cyclic symmetric function of the five roots proposed as one root of an auxiliary (resolvent) sextic
Table of the analogous sums $a^3xy+a^3zw$ under different permutations of the roots (the orbit of the resolvent function)
Differences of the permuted sums, factored by cubes of the roots
Expression in power sums / symmetric functions
Table of successive powers of decimal numbers

items.quote: Si a, b, c, d, e sint radices aequationis quinti gradus haec per solutionem binarum aequationum sexti gradus utriusque purae quinti inveniri possent. Alterius autem aequationis sexti gradus una radix erit
